preconditions.description: The input contains exactly n+1 lines, where the first line has n and S, and the next n lines describe the parcels.
The number of parcels n is between 1 and 500, and the platform strength S is between 0 and 1000.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= ini < outi < 2*n and 0 <= wi <= 1000 and 0 <= si <= 1000 and 1 <= vi <= 10**6 for ini, outi, wi, si, vi in parcels)
preconditions.description: For each parcel, the arrival time ini is strictly less than the delivery time outi, which is less than 2n; weight and strength are non-negative and at most 1000; value is positive and at most 10^6.

preconditions.expression: len(set((p[0], p[1]) for p in parcels)) == n
preconditions.description: All pairs of (arrival_time, delivery_time) are distinct.

postconditions.expression: isinstance(output, str) and output.strip().isdigit() and int(output.strip()) == max_total_value
postconditions.description: The output is a single non-negative integer representing the maximum total value achievable.

postconditions.expression: max_total_value == max(sum(v for i, v in enumerate(selected) if selected[i]), default=0) for selected in valid_selections
postconditions.description: The output equals the maximum sum of values of a subset of parcels that can be successfully processed according to the platform rules.

postconditions.expression: all(is_valid_schedule(selected, parcels, S) for selected in valid_selections)
postconditions.description: Every selection considered in the maximization corresponds to a valid schedule where all platform constraints (total weight <= S, box strength >= weight above) are satisfied at all times, respecting arrival and delivery times.
